You are running a numerical optimization campaign on four positions of an abstract four-position system.

DESIGN SPACE
Four positions, each holding one of 20 symbols (ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST).
A candidate is a 4-letter string, for example "GDIF".
Only a minority of the 160,000 possible candidates are viable. An order for a non-viable
candidate is rejected, and you will be asked for a replacement for that slot, up to
3 times. If every replacement is also non-viable, THE SLOT IS LOST and counts against
your budget. The reference point is "GDIF".

GOAL
Find the candidate with the highest score.

BUDGET
15 rounds, 4 orders per round, 60 measurements in total.
This is your entire budget and there is no way to get more.

HOW MEASUREMENT WORKS
- Each order returns a numeric score reading. The reference point reads about 6.87.
- About 15% of orders fail for technical reasons and return nothing. A failed order
  still consumes its slot.
- If your reply does not contain exactly the number of candidates asked for, you will be
  asked once more. If the second reply is also not exactly that number, THE WHOLE ROUND IS LOST
  and its slots count against your budget.
- Readings are subject to measurement error, so a reading is not exactly the
  candidate's true score.
- Each measurement carries independent Gaussian error whose standard deviation DEPENDS ON
  the string's own level f, as sigma(f) = sqrt(0.00351^2 + (0.073 * f)^2).
- You may order the same string more than once, within a round or across rounds.
- Independent measurements of the same string can be averaged; n measurements reduce the
  standard error of its mean by a factor of sqrt(n).
ROUND 1 OF 15. You have 60 measurements remaining.

HISTORY
(no measurements yet)

Choose 4 candidates to order this round.
Reply with exactly 4 lines and nothing else. Each line must be:
CANDIDATE | one short reason
for example:
ADIF | one short reason here
